title: FW: IP-1 Quarantine Order — Access Roads Disagree

fields.subject: FW: IP-1 quarantine order — address/barns/access CONFIRM BY 09:30
fields.note:
Ops, Sheriff, see the Prairie Gold reply below before anything goes back to the Board. It isn't complete.

The CR 12 bridge 0.4 mi east of the drive has been posted at 10 tons since August. Loaded feed and rendering trucks have been using the field lane off 230th Street to the north service gate. That makes TWO access points, and nobody gates the 230th lane.

My crew drove past it Thursday. There were fresh dual-axle ruts in the lane, so it's in regular use. If the order lists only the CR 12 drive, a rendering truck can come and go through the north gate and nobody will see it.

I can have a sign set and barricades at the 230th lane entrance within the hour if you want them. I'm on my cell all morning.
fields.signature:
Pete Vasquez
County Highway Engineer
Calder County Highway Department
555-0140

original.fromName: Larkin Ridge Turkey Complex — Brett Sandoval
original.to: Quarantine Officer, Minnesota Board of Animal Health
original.subject: RE: IP-1 quarantine order — address/barns/access CONFIRM BY 09:30
original.body:
2140 County Road 12, four barns. All trucks use the main drive off CR 12. That's the only way in.

Brett Sandoval
Complex Manager, Larkin Ridge Turkey Complex
Prairie Gold Turkey Cooperative

-----Original Message-----
From: Quarantine Officer, Minnesota Board of Animal Health
Sent: Tuesday, October 20, 2026 8:01 AM
To: Larkin Ridge Turkey Complex; Pete Vasquez; eoc-ops@caldercountymn.example
Subject: IP-1 quarantine order — address/barns/access CONFIRM BY 09:30

Please confirm the street address, barn count and every access road for IP-1 so the quarantine order can issue well before 11:50. We need one answer from the county by 09:30. Include any field lanes, service gates or seasonal approaches that trucks or crews actually use.

Quarantine Officer
Minnesota Board of Animal Health

instructorNote: This is a clue. The Board needs one confirmed answer, and the people closest to the farm disagree about it. Ops should call both people, confirm the two access points (the CR 12 drive and the 230th Street lane to the north gate), and send the Board one reconciled answer before 09:30. Watch whether the Sheriff plans security for both gates and marks the 230th lane as a priority checkpoint road for feed and rendering trucks.
